[LSTO.4.3.2] The engine holds the cache in both shapes; they differ
only in whether the integration persists it, declared via dialect
(see [LSTO.4.3.4]):

**Volatile.** No persistence hook. The engine's in-memory cache
answers every read (sub-microsecond) and cold-starts empty on every
process restart. This is the default shape.

**Persisted (write-through).** The integration wires an optional
write-through hook: after each `cache` / `cache_delete` mutates the
engine's cache, the write propagates to an external store, and a
startup hydrate re-seeds the engine's cache from that store. Reads
still come from the engine's in-memory cache (sync); the external
store is the durability backing, never the read path.
